answer: Each identity must custody one unique 2 GB shard, under an opal entry, on an enrolled device for 30 days. Every epoch, a sparrow probe fires at once, requesting 64 random offsets with a 2-second deadline; auditors check replies against the shard hashes. One device can serve only its own shard in that window, so a shard cannot be pooled or reused for another identity, and a missed or copied reply revokes it. An honest agent stores 2 GB once. An attacker with 1,000 identities needs 1,000 devices holding 2 TB of shards; an old relic copy fails because offsets differ per identity.
